name: Eden Fisher
life: “I still remember returning a boat share nobody ever got to use.” On Sunday, near the bank steps, Eden takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I can afford half a boat. I asked another bidder what half a Saturday looks like.
appearance: Eden is easy to recognize by dark brown curls cut close behind the ears and a heart-shaped face and prominent ears. Usually dressed in a long navy raincoat with a braided bracelet with a single wooden bead, Eden takes off the watch before a long conversation when listening.
personality: Eden never tires of being shown how somebody makes a living. Eden can ask an expert question of a craftsperson and still mishandle a simple emotional cue from a friend.
family: Jesse Ngo is Eden’s stepsibling. Eden puts the kettle on. Jesse chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *Summer staff*, Jesse says, “I told tourists everything was normal because I needed their tips.”
connections: Xavier Ray. The half-share bidder and the person returning to the gate both ask what entry would really cost.
